value.rationale: The continuation principle is a central tool for graph domination games, and its failure for the indicated total variant is known only in the inspected original via a larger cyclic example with multiple declarations. Establishing that the obstruction exists even on trees, with exactly one pre-dominated vertex, is structurally restrictive; proving the least possible order and uniqueness sharply locates the boundary. The elementary but infinite construction covers every larger tree order and distinguishes predomination monotonicity from the separate ordinary-game tree equality conjecture.
